**The claim is not supported by this data.** Checkout p95 latency on 2026-07-15 was about 392 ms, below 500 ms. The data only covers 00:00–19:59 UTC, though, so I can't rule out a breach in the last four hours of the day.

- **Daily p95:** 392.2 ms. Nearest-rank and linear interpolation give the same value.
- **Hourly p95:** the highest hour was 15:00 at 460 ms. The other 19 hours were between 321 and 437 ms, so no single hour reached 500 ms either.
- **Individual slow requests:** 14 of the 1,200 requests (about 1.2%) were over 500 ms, and the maximum was 708.7 ms (19:29). The claim may come from someone looking at max or outlier values rather than p95.
- **Data quality:** the file has 1,200 unique request IDs, one per minute, with no missing values and no other dates.

**Coverage gap:** the last timestamp is 19:59Z, so 20:00–23:59 is missing. Those hours would need an unusually bad stretch to lift the full-day p95 above 500 ms. That would take the slowest 5% of the day's requests being over 500 ms, and only 1.2% are so far. Rerun on the full day's export if you need a definitive answer.

**Timezone:** I treated "yesterday" as 2026-07-15 UTC, as the timestamps are in UTC.

The script is `/var/folders/4_/s6fbcjyn4b13xdxkd3lv0kw00000gn/T/arm-s11-baseline-v0t79kx1/work/a.py`.
